newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr rattled as rate doubts stir anew.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr rattled as rate doubts stir anew.

text.p: The Australian dollar wobbled at the midsession after surprisingly weak retail sales data gave bulls a bad case of deja vu.

Sales slid 1.8 percent in June, the biggest drop in nine months, confounding forecasts of a 0.4 percent rise. This continued a volatile pattern which saw a rise of 2.2 percent in May and a fall of 1.7 percent in April. For Q2 real sales were off 0.5 percent implying a detraction from GDP growth.
It was the April fall which first started the speculation which culminated in Wednesday's rate cut and bulls were worried the June weakness would start the whole process again.

By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the dollar was putting a brave face on the figures at US$0.7445/50 having rallied from a US$0.7433 low hit immediately after the release aided by bids from exporters who missed Tuesday's offshore surge.
It had started at US$0.7435/40 after finishing Wednesday at US$0.7460/65 having proved resilient to the reality of lower interest rates after weeks of anticipation.

Part of the equanimity was due to the general assumption official rates had bottomed at 5.0 percent and there was enough monetary stimulus in the pipeline to assure a pickup in growth to the four percent level needed to curb unemployment.
That was still the feeling of most analysts, although the dire sales data illustrated the trouble the dollar was likely to have sustaining a recovery in the medium term.

The softness of spending suggested consumers remained reluctant to splash out while unemployment stayed so high and could have been waiting for the winter sales which came in July this year instead of June.

If so sales could rebound in July but analysts reckoned it would take a string of stronger employment numbers before consumers felt secure enough about their jobs to spend more. That would make next week's labour report all the more crucial.
Analysts feel employment is overdue a big bounce after disappointing weakness in recent months but the volatility of the series is such that noone was confident of strength.

They noted the fall in mortgage rates triggered by the rate cut of May 23 had only been passed on to existing bank customers today and most of the reductions announced Wednesday were not scheduled to take effect until September.

All this made most think the Reserve Bank would wait to assess the data over at least the next two months before deciding if a sixth easing was actually needed. In the interim the dollar would be vulnerable to every bad figure.
Treasurer Peter Costello tried to put a gloss on the data saying spending was solid and over the course of the year sales had been strengthening in trend terms.
Trend sales were up 0.1 percent in June having slowed from 0.6 percent in February.

On the crosses the dollar was steady on early levels at 88.05/15 yen but off on Wednesday's late 88.74/84. It also lost a little of its recent gains on the mark to 1.3678/95 from 1.3723/45 -- which had been the highest close in more than five years -- and was unchanged in trade weighted terms at 58.3.
